**Section D: Composition Writing (10 marks).** Choose ONE topic from below and write an essay of between 250-300 words.

**Topic 1.** You have just passed the BACC exam and want to volunteer your services at your local council. Write a letter of application to the Mayor of the council in Eding, explaining what you desire to do and why, the benefits it will bring to your community, the council and yourself. Your name and address is Angele Abong, GBHS Eding, P.O. Box 2033.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A évalue à la fois le respect du format imposé (lettre formelle, essai d'opinion, discours) et la qualité du contenu. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés.

## Topic 1 - Formal letter (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Angele Abong
GBHS Eding
P.O. Box 2033

The Mayor
Eding Council

Subject: Application to volunteer at the council

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to express my strong desire to volunteer my services at Eding Council, having recently passed my Baccalaureate examination.

Throughout my time at GBHS Eding, I developed a genuine interest in community service, particularly in areas such as youth mobilisation, record-keeping and public communication. I would like to put these skills to good use while contributing meaningfully to the development of our council during this period before I pursue further studies.

I believe such volunteering would bring several benefits. For the council, I could assist with administrative tasks, help organise community outreach activities, and support ongoing council initiatives at no cost to the institution. For our community, an engaged and visible youth volunteer could help encourage other young people to take a more active interest in local governance. For myself, this experience would allow me to gain practical administrative and interpersonal skills, build professional relationships, and better understand how local government functions, all of which would be valuable regardless of the career path I eventually pursue.

I am available to begin immediately and can commit to a flexible schedule that suits the council's needs. I would be glad to discuss this further at your convenience, and I have attached my Baccalaureate certificate for your reference.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to your favourable response.

Yours faithfully,

Angele Abong

**Section D: Composition Writing (10 marks).** Choose ONE topic from below and write an essay of between 250-300 words.

**Topic 2.** You so much desire to travel abroad after you pass the BACC exam. Your grandmother advises you to stay back and says, "home is home." Write an essay in which you explain what this means. Explain with reasons whether you agree or disagree with this mass emigration.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Opinion essay (modèle, environ 270 mots)

When my grandmother told me, "home is home," after I expressed my strong desire to travel abroad following my Baccalaureate exam, I initially dismissed it as an old-fashioned saying. Looking more closely at what it truly means, however, I find myself largely, though not entirely, in agreement with her.

"Home is home" suggests that no matter how attractive life abroad may appear, nothing can fully replace the sense of belonging, identity and rootedness one finds in one's own country, among one's own people, culture and family. It is a reminder that a place is not valuable merely for its material comfort, but for the relationships and meaning it holds for us.

I agree with this view to a significant extent. Many young Cameroonians who emigrate in search of a better life often discover, once abroad, that they are treated as outsiders, face discrimination, or struggle in jobs far below their qualifications, all while missing the community and support system they left behind. Mass emigration, particularly when pursued through illegal and dangerous means, has cost many young lives and torn families apart, often for a future that does not materialise as imagined.

At the same time, I do not believe one must never leave home. Studying, working or gaining experience abroad, pursued legally and with a clear purpose, can bring skills and opportunities back home that benefit both the individual and the country.

In conclusion, "home is home" does not mean we should never leave; it means that wherever we go, we should remember what makes home worth returning to, and be cautious about abandoning it recklessly.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D: Composition Writing (10 marks).** Choose ONE topic from below and write an essay of between 250-300 words.

**Topic 3.** You are the president of the English club in your school. It is the Bilingualism Week and you have to address the youths on the theme "Bilingualism, the bedrock of unity and multiculturalism." Write a speech that explains this theme and elaborates on the benefits of bilingualism. Your name is Amina Ottou and your school is GBHS Akata.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Speech (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Ladies and gentlemen, fellow youths,

As president of the English Club, I am honoured to address you today, during Bilingualism Week, on a theme that lies at the very heart of our national identity: "Bilingualism, the bedrock of unity and multiculturalism."

Cameroon's bilingual character, inherited from its unique colonial history, is often treated as a mere administrative requirement — a subject to pass rather than a strength to embrace. I stand before you today to argue the opposite: our bilingualism is one of our greatest national assets.

First, bilingualism fosters unity. When an English-speaking Cameroonian can converse comfortably in French, and a French-speaking Cameroonian can do the same in English, invisible barriers between our two major linguistic communities begin to dissolve, replaced by mutual understanding and shared national belonging.

Second, bilingualism celebrates multiculturalism. Rather than forcing one culture to dominate the other, our system, at its best, allows both Anglophone and Francophone traditions to coexist and enrich one another, creating a uniquely Cameroonian identity shaped by both.

Third, bilingualism offers real, practical advantages: greater access to regional and international opportunities, stronger cognitive and communication skills, and a distinct edge in an increasingly interconnected job market.

Fellow youths, let us stop viewing bilingualism as a burden imposed on us, and start seeing it as the bridge that connects us to one another and to the wider world.

Thank you.

### Piège à éviter
Sur le sujet 2, l'erreur fréquente est de se contenter de paraphraser la citation "home is home" sans jamais prendre clairement position (accord/désaccord) comme l'exige la consigne : un essai d'opinion doit toujours affirmer une thèse claire, même nuancée.

### Conseil
Pour un sujet demandant explicitement d'expliquer le sens d'une citation puis de donner son avis, consacre un paragraphe séparé à chacune de ces deux tâches : cela garantit qu'aucune partie de la consigne n'est oubliée.
